metaTitle: Mercedes Cylinder Head Repair & Rebuild | Mercedes Garage
metaDescription: Precision cylinder head repair and rebuild for all Mercedes-Benz engines. Full disassembly, machining, valve train overhaul, and reassembly with genuine parts.
lede: Precision cylinder head overhaul for all Mercedes-Benz petrol and diesel engines - from 4-cylinder to V12. Full disassembly, machine-shop work, valve train service, and reassembly with OEM-spec parts.

sections.heading: What Cylinder Head Repair & Rebuild Involves

steps.title: Access & Removal
steps.body: Engine cooled, battery disconnected, coolant and oil drained. All ancillaries, intake, exhaust, turbochargers (where fitted), and timing components are carefully removed. The head is lifted using a fixture after timing is locked.

steps.title: Full Disassembly
steps.body: Valves, springs, retainers, hydraulic lifters, and valve guides are stripped. Each component is inspected and measured against factory tolerances.

steps.title: Machining & Valve Work
steps.body: Heads are checked for flatness (max 0.1mm warpage) and resurfaced if needed (max 0.2mm removal). Valve seats are machined with 45° + correction angles, guides replaced, and valve-to-seat sealing verified with a vacuum tester.

steps.title: Reassembly & Testing
steps.body: New valve stem seals, lifters (if required), and all gaskets are fitted. Cylinder head bolts **must** be replaced - they are torque-to-yield and single-use. Reassembly follows the Mercedes-spec torque sequence with angle-tightening, and timing is reset using factory locking tools.

sections.heading: Our Cylinder Head Rebuild Process - In Detail

steps.title: Inspection & Diagnosis
steps.body: We visually inspect the head and perform a leak test if the engine is still assembled. We assess the extent of work needed: valve guide wear, seat condition, and flatness.

steps.title: Stripping & Cleaning
steps.body: All components are removed and cleaned in a thermal cleaning oven to remove carbon deposits. Valves, guides, and springs are laid out for measurement.

steps.title: Machining & Resurfacing
steps.body: Heads are checked for warpage with a straight edge; resurfaced if within tolerance (max 0.2mm removal). Valve seats are machined to correct angles, and guides are replaced if worn.

steps.title: Valve Train Overhaul
steps.body: New valve stem seals, springs, and hydraulic lifters (where required) are installed. Valve-to-seat sealing is verified with a vacuum test.

steps.title: Reassembly & Timing
steps.body: New TTY head bolts are installed and tightened in the correct sequence with angle torque. Timing is set using factory locking tools. All gaskets and seals are replaced.

steps.title: Final Testing & Adaptation
steps.body: After reassembly, the engine is filled with fresh Mercedes-approved oil and coolant. We run the engine, check for leaks, and use Mercedes-Benz Star Diagnostic (Xentry) to clear codes and run adaptations.

items.q: What does a cylinder head rebuild involve?
items.a: A full rebuild includes removal, disassembly, cleaning, resurfacing (if needed), valve seat machining, valve guide replacement, new valve stem seals, hydraulic lifters (if required), reassembly with new TTY head bolts, timing setting, and final testing with Mercedes-Star Diagnostic.

items.q: Which Mercedes engines are most complex for cylinder head work?
items.a: V12 engines (e.g. M275) have individual timing chains per bank, heavy heads (~80-90 lbs), and require more ancillary removal. V8 biturbo engines (M157/M177/M278) are tightly packaged, adding complexity. All modern Mercedes engines require torque-to-yield bolts and multi-stage angle tightening.

items.q: What specialist tools do you use for this repair?
items.a: We use Mercedes-specific timing chain locking tools, camshaft locking tools, torque angle gauges, cylinder head lifting fixtures, and a range of metric thread chasers. We also use a precision straight edge and feeler gauges for flatness checks, and a vacuum tester for valve sealing.

items.q: Do you replace cylinder head bolts every time?
items.a: Yes. All modern Mercedes cylinder head bolts are torque-to-yield (TTY) and must be replaced with new ones on every reassembly. Reusing them risks head gasket failure.
Yes. We use Mercedes-Benz Star Diagnostic System (Xentry) to clear fault codes, run adaptations, and verify system readiness after the head is refitted.
